items.message: `getattr(commands, 'executables', ())` is called twice on separate code paths with the same object; the two reads could diverge if `commands` is mutable, but more practically the pattern is repeated rather than extracted.
The `asyncio.run()` call inside `_probe_executables` will raise `RuntimeError` if an event loop is already running (e.g. when `doctor` is called from an async context).

Top-level import of a private name (`_sandbox_executables`) inside `_doctor_over` is a module-level import placed mid-file after test functions, breaking the conventional import grouping the rest of the file follows.
Program names from ALLOWED_COMMANDS are interpolated into a shell script without quoting.
Module-level import of a private symbol mid-file is fragile and bypasses the fixture-free import guard at the top of the file.
_Image.run models shell exit-code semantics, but the assertion it protects is only checked via the doctor path, not via _probe_executables directly.
test_gate_script_1_doctor_says_what_to_declare_when_nothing_is_declared asserts a specific tuple string that depends on ALLOWED_COMMANDS ordering.
No test asserts the doctor NOTE for the 'unlisted' branch (image carries a program that executables= omits).
